stops.note: to prick, to pierce, combined with com- (thoroughly)
to prick sharply, to sting the conscience, from com- and pungere
stops.meaning: to prick sharply, to sting the conscience

stops.note: a pricking of conscience, remorse, from compungere
settled as the English word for a feeling of guilt about one's actions
stops.meaning: a feeling of guilt or unease about one's actions

current_meaning: a feeling of guilt or moral unease about doing something
